about: What a finding's citations are resolved against, as DATA. A `cites-resolve` check names one resolver here; the resolver's `kind` is one of three ways of looking something up (file-line, commit, row), its `pattern` finds the citations in a text, and `roots` names the repositories by the name a citation starts with. A root lists its `sources` in the order they are tried: `{folder, ref}` is a checkout on the computer running the check (read with git at the ref), `{files}` is a folder of the person's own files holding a copy of the source (read through the files door, so a run in a container with a files right reads it too). The copy folder holds `.source-copy.json` ({ref, copied_at}), the files at their paths, and `.commit-dates.json` ({ <commit hash>: <ISO date> }). A root with no source available here makes the check unevaluated, never passed. A `row` resolver lists the row `types` it may read; the tool row declares a read right for exactly those types. Adding a repository, a copy folder or a row type is adding a row here.

resolvers.meaning: <root>/<path>:<line>; the line of the file at the root's ref must hold the quoted text when the check names a quote field.
A commit hash; it must exist in one of the roots and be dated after the date the check's `after` field holds.
A row id in the person's own records; the row must exist.
